gen-fs-sharpie-general-sans: General Sans fills the line with a tall, smooth-curving sans under a heading that nearly shuts every letter. And Sharpie's squeezed, bold shapes against those open curves are what make the pair memorable.
gen-fs-sharpie-gf-orbit: Orbit lets its curves stop short, each character floating free. Under Sharpie's bold, nearly sealed letters, that openness gives the layout a loud voice on top and a drifting one below.
gen-fs-sharpie-gf-science-gothic: Tight shut above, spaced out below. Sharpie nearly seals its bold letters, while Science Gothic keeps stroke ends far apart in a uniform line, and that opposition is the draw.
gen-fs-sharpie-gf-syncopate: Syncopate reads like technical drawing, steady and open. Above it, Sharpie's bold heading pinches nearly shut, so the two trade a tight squeeze for rungs of open spacing below.
gen-fs-sharpie-manrope: Manrope reads bright, its curves opening wide at every mouth. Against Sharpie's bold, almost sealed shapes, that brightness is the pairing's best trick, a tight heading over a body that breathes.
gen-fs-sharpie-montserrat: Sharpie packs its bold letters so tight that only a hairline gap survives inside each one. But Montserrat, a sans-serif with oversized, generous counters, gives all that pressure somewhere to exhale.
gen-fs-sharpie-satoshi: Sharpie's bold, expressive letters close up almost completely, leaving the thinnest crack of light inside each shape. Satoshi then loosens everything below, drawing tall, uniform strokes that stay open.
gen-fs-sharpie-switzer: Tight bold heading, lanky wire-like text: Sharpie nearly seals its letters while Switzer stands tall. And paragraphs in Switzer should move smoothly, its tubular forms and untouching c tips keeping the eye gliding.
gen-fs-sharpie-work-sans: Pinched heading, bent-paperclip body text. Sharpie nearly seals each bold letter, while Work Sans lays down modern, unswollen strokes under a high mean line, so paragraphs read smoothly.
